registerBackend.step1: 1. Visit <linkReleases>LLaMA.cpp releases</linkReleases> and download a prebuilt binary for your hardware.
registerBackend.step1note: Note: You can also git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git into a folder and build from source. See Recipes Guide.
registerBackend.step2: 2. Open the <linkBackends>Backends page</linkBackends> and add a new backend.
registerBackend.step3: 3. Open the file picker, navigate to the llama.cpp folder you downloaded and unzipped, then select the llama-server binary.
registerBackend.step4: 4. Save the backend. It should auto-validate your system and detect the hardware.

loadModel.title_todo: Download a Model from HuggingFace and Add it
loadModel.step1: 1. Go to <linkSettings>Settings</linkSettings> and select the folder where you want to keep your GGUF model files (if not already chosen).
loadModel.step3: 3. Search for a model family name such as Qwen, Mistral, or Gemma.
loadModel.step4: 4. Click on a model from the results list on the left panel. Choose a model released in the last 6 months for best capabilities.
loadModel.step4note: Note: Llama Models are different from Whisper Models. For whisper, search for "ggml" .bin models.
loadModel.step5: 5. On the right panel, open the dropdown for model files, and choose a quantized GGUF file that can fit into your VRAM with some space left over.
loadModel.step6: 6. Click download. The download progress window will be shown. You can pause and resume large downloads.
loadModel.step7: 7. Once download finishes, navigate to the <linkModels>Models</linkModels> page and click Rescan Models button to add the model.

createServer.step3: 3. Select the model you added from the dropdown list of models.
createServer.step4: 4. Select the backend you registered from the dropdown list of backends.
createServer.step5: 5. Select the device to load the model on.
createServer.step6: 6. Configure params such as context length, number of threads, and GPU layers. Adjust these based on your hardware - more GPU layers means faster inference but requires more VRAM.
createServer.step7: 7. Click Launch to start the server.
